entry.title: Your Polymarket Bot Has Live Prices. That Doesn't Mean It Has the Latest Order Book.
entry.summary: A trading bot can receive price updates every second and still make decisions using a market state that no longer exists. That sounds contradictory until you look at how an order book changes. A bot sees an attractive ask, calculates an edge, and prepares an order. Before that order reaches the exchange, someone cancels the liquidity, another trader takes the offer, or the best available price changes. The bot's calculation may have been correct when it started. The market it calculated against is gone. This is one of the problems that separates a bot that merely consumes market data from one that handles live trading conditions properly. entry.title: Room 3 froze on a suspending @Transaction: the SQLite driver you pass picks your connection pool
entry.summary: Short answer: Room 3 does not manage connections the same way for every driver. It reads the hasConnectionPool property off whatever SQLiteDriver you pass to setDriver(), and that single boolean picks the concurrency model. AndroidSQLiteDriver returns true, so Room wraps it in PassthroughConnectionPool, which holds one thread-confined connection and has no acquisition timeout at all. A suspending @Transaction DAO function on that pool can block forever: the main thread stays idle, so there is no ANR, no crash, and no log line. Swapping to BundledSQLiteDriver makes Room run its own pool instead, and Room configures PRAGMA synchronous on every connection it opens, which quietly discards anything you set in RoomDatabase.Callback.onOpen. entry.title: Image Metadata Privacy Leaks: EXIF, GPS & Thumbnails
entry.summary: A photo is two things: the pixels you chose to share, and a block of metadata you probably never looked at. The pixels are reviewed. The metadata is not, and it can carry the GPS position where the shot was taken, the exact device that took it, a timestamp with your timezone offset, your name from an editing app, and sometimes a small preview of the uncropped original. I build privacy and developer tools at PixelValut, and this is the leak I most often find in otherwise careful people's files. entry.title: Building a Battery Management System (BMS) Core in Rust
entry.summary:
Every lithium-ion battery you use, from a phone to an EV, has a small piece of software and hardware babysitting it. That is the Battery Management System (BMS). Without one, a pack can overcharge, overheat, or drift out of balance, and the failure modes range from a dead pack to a fire. In this post I'll cover what a BMS does and then build a minimal BMS core in Rust.
A BMS has four main jobs: Monitoring: it measures the voltage of each cell, the pack current, and temperatures. State estimation: it estimates State of Charge (SoC, "how full is it?") and State of Health (SoH, "how worn out is it?"). Protection: it opens the contactor or MOSFET when something goes out of range (over-voltage, under-voltage, over-temperature, over-current). Balancing: cells in series drift apart over time, so…
